pr.title: Answer an agent's questions from Projector's band
pr.head: 51e8c80b9ebcefb4a1c53bc2960358219789bde4

summary: When a review or fix loop's subagent needs a decision from you, it can only hand the question to the main loop, which asks it as a line in the transcript. That line scrolls away, and your answer has no route back to the subagent. The questions plan fixes this in two pull requests. The first, #271, now merged into main, added project question, a command any host can run to ask, list, answer, and deliver questions. This second one builds Claude Code's view on top of that command, in Projector's band, the strip above the prompt that lists the pull requests your loops track.
The change gives Claude Code three things:

1. An ask tool. The model sees it as mcp__projector__ask from the first turn. The hooks module serves it by running project question ask, so a question asked through the tool and one asked from the shell land in the same store. The tool returns the question's reference, such as #337.3, at once, and the agent keeps working.
  2. Questions in the band. Each question sits on the line after the pull request it is about. Clicking its reference opens a drawer with the detail, the lettered answers (a is always the agent's recommendation), a field for a typed answer, and dismiss.
  3. Delivery. The band records your answer through the CLI, then claims it and sends it: straight to the asking subagent while that subagent is still live, or otherwise to the main loop as a prompt of its own. A reference you type in the prompt, such as go with #337.3.b, reaches the agent with its question attached.
The plan stays in-progress. One acceptance row, opening a question's drawer on the main screen with ctrl+x tab and Enter, is a check by hand under tmux that has not been done.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• The store: project question's files for one session, one JSON file per question under $XDG_STATE_HOME/projector/questions/<session>/.
  • Reference: a question's fixed name, #337.3, owner/repo#337.3, or q2; an answer adds its letter, as #337.3.a.
  • Claim: a random token a deliverer takes on a recorded answer, so only one deliverer sends it. A claim lapses after a minute without renewal.
  • Route: send, a message to a live subagent through $.session.send, or submit, a prompt for the main loop through $.prompt.submit, which waits until the session is idle.
  • Signature: a string built from the store directory's file names, sizes and times, which the band compares on each tick to decide whether to read the store again.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, at f1229f3, found one P2 defect: the band recorded a new signature before its store read ran, so a read that failed was not retried until the directory changed again.
  • At 7236879 the commit was rebased, unchanged, onto #271's new head, and the finding stayed open.
  • At 51e8c80, after #271 merged, the pull request targets main. Two commits fix the finding: the signature is recorded only after a read succeeds, and a project call that does not finish tells the agent to ask in the conversation rather than to upgrade. The review of this head is clean.
  • The gate passed at this head: 881 Python tests, project check, both claude plugin validate runs, and 44 hook tests under claude plugin test.

groups.title: The state and the pure helpers
groups.kicker: The types the band keeps and the logic that needs no engine
intro: Two files hold everything that can be tested without the engine. hooks/types.d.ts declares a Question as project question list --json prints it, and the two pieces of session state the band adds: bandQuestions, the band's last read of the store, and bandSending, each delivery in flight.

hooks/questions.ts holds the decisions: which text might hold a reference, which letter is the typed answer, whether an answer still needs a deliverer, which route an answer takes, where the store lives, the directory signature, the order the band draws questions in, and the ask tool's description, schema, and arguments.

checks.text: Session state survives a hot reload of the hooks module, while module variables do not. That is why each delivery's token, route, and text live in bandSending: a reloaded module can keep renewing a submit an earlier copy made, and recognize its prompt when it arrives.

files.note: Adds Question, Answer, and Sending, and the bandQuestions and bandSending state keys.

checks.text: bandSending is keyed by reference alone. That holds because the band only delivers questions from its own session's store.

files.note: The engine-free helpers: reference detection, letters, delivery need, routing, the store path and signature, ordering, and the tool's schema and argument vector.

checks.text: These statuses match the engine's AgentStatus in the 2.1.296 plugin-authoring declarations, which lists completed, failed, and killed as the ended states.
A file whose claim the band itself renews counts by name alone, so the band's renewal every 5 seconds does not make it run project question list again. Any other change to the directory does.

I ran the vector this builds against the CLI in a temporary state directory: a question and a recommendation that start with - stay text, a --detail value keeps its line break, and the store records each value as given.

groups.title: The tool, the store read, and delivery
groups.kicker: How the hooks module asks, reads, records, and delivers
intro: hooks/register.tsx wires the helpers into the engine. At session.start it registers the ask tool with isDeferred: false, so its schema is in the model's tool list from the first turn. Its tool.call hook runs project question ask and answers with the reference, or refuses with { deny }: the check that failed for exit 65, or the error and run project upgrade for any other exit.

Every 5-second tick, shown or hidden, the band lists the store's directory and runs project question list only when the signature changed. A question it has not shown before shows the band. Then the band renews each claim it holds and starts delivering each recorded answer nobody is delivering:

1. Claim. project question claim prints a token and the text to send. A non-zero exit means another deliverer holds it.
  2. Send or submit. A subagent that $.agent.list() reports as live gets the text through $.session.send. Otherwise, or when the send is not delivered, the main loop gets it through $.prompt.submit, with a line naming the subagent that asked.
  3. Settle. A delivered send or an entered submit runs project question delivered. A dropped submit, or a call that fails, runs reopen and raises a toast, so the question is open again.

The band's own prompt.submit hook also settles a submit when it arrives, so a submit made by a copy of the module that a hot reload replaced still settles. The same hook attaches project question context's output to a prompt that types a reference. The rest of the file draws each question's line and drawer.

checks.text: I checked each engine call against the 2.1.296 plugin-authoring declarations: $.tool.register with isDeferred, the tool.call answer as { result } or { deny }, SessionSendResult.isDelivered, PromptSubmitResult.drop, $.fs.list's entries, and a mobile surface without Input.

files.note: Registers and serves ask, reads the store on every tick, records answers from the drawer, claims and delivers them, attaches typed references, and draws the questions.

checks.text: The signature is recorded only after the read succeeds. A failed list returns early and unparseable JSON throws, so the next tick reads again. A band test whose first list exits 1 delivers the waiting answer at this head and leaves it undelivered without this change.

Settling takes the entry out of bandSending in one state update before it runs the CLI. Whichever of the submit's own result and the prompt.submit hook comes second finds the entry gone and does nothing.

A send that a replaced copy of the module left is dropped here, so its claim lapses and the band delivers the answer again a minute later. A submit keeps being renewed, because it still waits in the session's queue.
A prompt from this plugin is the band's own submit arriving. The hook matches it to a bandSending entry by its text and marks it delivered.

Letters and references are Buttons with no hotkey: Claude Code presses a band button whose hotkey is a digit when that digit is typed first in an empty prompt, so a hotkey would let 2 things first: answer a question.
A call that rejects, because project could not start or was still running at the 15-second timeout, no longer tells the agent to upgrade. It tells the agent to ask in the conversation instead.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The helpers alone, and the band driven through the engine's test kit
intro: hooks/questions.test.ts covers the helpers directly. hooks/band.test.tsx drives the whole module through the engine's test kit, over an in-memory stand-in for project question that keeps questions, claims, and tokens the way the CLI does.

checks.text: claude plugin test . passed all 44 tests at this head. Run over the first commit's register.tsx, the new retry and timeout tests fail.

files.note: Reference detection, letters, the minute a delivered question stays, claim lapse, routing by status, the store path, the signature, ordering, and the tool's arguments.

Asking through the tool, the three refusals (a failed check, an old CLI, and a call that does not finish), a hidden band shown by a shell question, an idle session starting no process, each answer kind and route, a dropped submit, a renewed claim through a long turn, a failed store read retried on the next tick, a reload's leftover submit, and a typed reference.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: What users read about the band, and what the plan now records
intro: docs/plugins.md gains a section on answering questions in the band. The plan's § 2.6, § 2.7, § 2.8, and § 5 now record two decisions this layer made: the Input is keyed by its answer's reference and left out on mobile, and each delivery lives in bandSending so a hot reload cannot send a second copy.
